body (anything more than a bare expr — the moment ls_push_scope fires
inside lower_expr_body's BlockExpr arm) trapped at offset 144 OOB on

mentl/65b5824:
The Rust VM's push builtin was cloning the entire list on every call because
Arc refcount stayed > 1.  Three root causes, three fixes:

1. Progressive frame scanning: when push fires, walk call frames downward
   clearing ptr-equal list aliases until refcount reaches 1.  This handles
   recursive functions (lex_from) and intermediate call chains (unify_types
   → subst_set → push) that held stale references.

2. Evidence dispatch cleanup: op_perform_evidence no longer holds a Rust-
   local clone of handler state during nested execute(), eliminating an
   invisible Arc reference the VM's COW scan couldn't reach.

3. Consistent push usage: changed [entry] ++ env to push(env, entry) in
   lower.lux to eliminate non-linear list patterns that conflicted with
   aggressive alias clearing.

Also: named handler state in check.lux (6 individual variables instead of
one tuple), subst_bind/subst_apply effects in Infer for direct handler-arm
push (no intermediate frames), and dispatch stack refactoring (resume
metadata moved from VmHandlerFrame to HandlerDispatchEntry).

Results:
  lux check wasm_check.lux: 11.7GB → 70MB (167x), 2:20 → 1:31
  lux wasm wasm_check.lux:  14GB → 58MB (240x), 3:56 → 1:48
  wasm_bootstrap.lux:       OOM → 92MB, 12:43 (full compiler to WASM)

mentl/65fdfca:
Every LowExpr variant now carries its resolved Ty as the first field.
The structural invariant: you cannot construct an untyped LowExpr.
lower_expr attaches types inline by reading .ty off recursively-lowered
children via lexpr_ty. No separate inference pass, no sidecar maps.

Deleted (the redundant type re-inference):
- lower.lux: inferred_type, infer_concat_type, infer_type_list (57 lines)
- wasm_emit.lux: wasm_type_of, local_wasm_type, find_let_type,
  find_let_type_list (57 lines)
- emit_binop: fAdd/fSub/... prefix convention — now dispatches on
  (operand_ty, op) directly

Fixed:
- lower_lambda_named: extends env with parameter types from the
  function's TFun signature BEFORE lowering the body. This is the
  single change that makes x : TFloat reach VarRef("x") inside a fn
  body. Without it, parameter types died at scope boundaries and
  downstream code defaulted to TUnit/i32.
- extend_env_from_stmt: no longer shadows FnStmt names with TUnit —
  the checker's real TFun stays in env.
- infer_binop: no longer eagerly commits operands to TInt when both
  sides are still TVars. Defers to later unification. Fixes tanh_approx
  which committed x : TInt via `x * x` before seeing float literals.
- wasm globals: emit_global_decls reads Ty from env → emits
  `(global $y (mut f32) (f32.const 0))` for TFloat globals.
- closure captures: emit_closure_captures_stacked reads lexpr_ty of
  each capture and emits f32.store/i32.store accordingly. LUpval load
  dispatches on its Ty field for f32.load/i32.load.
- lower_closure.map_to_globals_typed: captures look up their real
  type in env (not TUnit) so the store/load dispatch works.

ARCHITECTURE.md says intelligence is compression per joule but never
says compress what. This document supplies the missing object: the
past, compressed into state, keeping exactly the bits the future will
bill for. The derivation runs from the gap between marginal entropy
and entropy rate, through Takens embedding and predictive information
(the future-relevant bits of a stream grow sublinearly -- the needle
in the entropy haystack), to causal states as the limit object of
crystallization and prediction as synchronization of observer with
source.

It ships with receipts rather than promises: the regime instrument's
first measurement (random core at lambda1 = -1.23 nats/token, memory
horizon 0.8 tokens -- the reservoir probe's null result explained
mechanically), the first four modules ever crystallized from real
pipeline flow (causal partition, same episodes state-only clustering
took to zero), and a latent 10^12-op search bug the first module
exposed and its same-day fix.

Bets 6-8 are pre-registered under the Part V discipline: causal
partition vs state-only at equal compute on a trained core (Bet 6),
Spearman correlation between lambda1 and held-out NLL across Path B
checkpoints (Bet 7), and horizon-weighted loss vs next-token-only for
the future train command (Bet 8). Bet 7 is written so its own
instrument can kill the edge-of-chaos story for this architecture --
selective-state models partly earn their keep by forgetting on
purpose, and if a capable trained core stays deeply contractive, Part
III gets rewritten by its own dial.

Cross-references: ARCHITECTURE.md status notes the two-document bet
registry, IF_FOUND.md records the mechanism behind the probe verdict
it already reported, PLAN.md gains the attractor track (explicitly
instrumentation for Path B, not a detour from it).
